solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Change direction with this winning performance?

definitions.text: Change direction with this winning performance?

parts.words: Change direction with this winning performance?
parts.note: a winning performance in football earns three points, and a performance can also be a turn; the manoeuvre itself reverses a car's direction

explanation.surface: A sports report about a team that turned its season around with a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: A football win is worth three points and a stage act is a 'turn', so 'winning performance' reads as a three-point turn: the road manoeuvre for reversing direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The driving manoeuvre of forward, reverse, forward is the standard way to turn a car round in a narrow road.

clue.text: Put on trial in seclusion after rising? That's not right

indicators.note: That's not right says the abbreviation for right must be dropped
in a down clue rising means the word for seclusion is read from bottom to top

parts.note: purdah is the practice of keeping women secluded from public view

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled into court while living as a recluse, and protests it is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns PURDAH into HADRUP; 'not' then removes the R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had up is British idiom for being brought before a court, i.e. charged and tried.

clue.text: Catch accomplice heading north after losing tail

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means the remaining letters are read upwards, back to front
after losing tail says the accomplice word first sheds its final letter, before anything else happens

parts.note: a partner in crime is an accomplice

explanation.surface: A detective catches a criminal's sidekick fleeing northward after the gang lost its pursuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing tail' drops the last letter of PARTNER; 'heading north' then turns the rest upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them, especially by a trick or snare.

clue.text: Spice among five in vegetable tea is sweet

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: in says the Spice Girl is placed inside the vegetable and tea combination

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Mel B was one of the five Spice Girls, the 1990s pop group

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a spice mixed into a tea flavoured with vegetables comes out sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a five-member British pop group; Mel B (Scary Spice) was one of them. Her name goes inside PEA + CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The dessert of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce is a sweet, the British word for pudding.

clue.text: Finger losing tip becomes black

indicators.note: losing tip says the finger word sheds its opening letter to leave the colour

parts.note: the pinky is the little finger
the tip of the finger word is its first letter, which is the one removed

explanation.surface: A finger that has lost its tip turns black, as with frostbite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tip' signals the deletion of the finger word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like ink is very dark, so the adjective means black, as in the inky night.

clue.text: Tease husband having little sense up top

indicators.note: in a down clue up top places the little sense above the husband

parts.note: toy describes something miniature, as in a toy poodle
wit is good sense or intelligence
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wife teases a husband who has not much brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up top' puts TOY + WIT above H in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with someone's feelings or treat them lightly is to tease them.

clue.text: Student grant provider ditches fellow, degree unfinished

indicators.note: ditches says the abbreviation for fellow is thrown out of the provider word

parts.note: a body that gives grants is a funder

indicators.note: unfinished tells us the degree word loses its last letter

parts.note: a grade is a degree or level

explanation.surface: A funding body drops a fellowship and the student's degree is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditches' takes F out of FUNDER; 'unfinished' cuts GRADE to GRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student who has not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: Show signs of hesitation after breaking spindle, but don't give up

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sounds behind the rearranged spindle
breaking says the letters of spindle are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: er and um are the sounds people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: Someone dithers after a spinning-wheel part snaps, but is urged to persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns SPINDLE into NILDESP; ER AND UM follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means never despair, an exhortation to keep going rather than abandon hope.

clue.text: What's kept by phlegmatic chap with a frozen handlebar?

definitions.text: What's kept by phlegmatic chap with a frozen handlebar?

parts.words: What's kept by phlegmatic chap with a frozen handlebar?
parts.note: an unemotional Briton keeps a resolute bearing, and a handlebar moustache frozen solid makes the skin under it rigid too

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a stoical gent whose moustache has iced over.
explanation.walkthrough: A handlebar is a wide curled moustache; frozen, it would literally stiffen the lip beneath it, while 'keeping' one is the idiom for stoicism.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's emotions hidden in adversity is the idiom's meaning, the stereotype of British stoicism.

clue.text: Cites dark manoeuvring to throw off the scent

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests moving pieces around, so the letters of cites dark are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quotes obscure material cleverly to mislead pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges CITES DARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone from their intended path or purpose is to mislead them, as a hunted animal confuses hounds.

clue.text: Broadcast melody off mountain-top?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters left are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the top of the word mountain is its first letter, M, which comes off the melody

explanation.surface: Reads like a radio listing for a tune transmitted from a hilltop mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes M (the top of 'mountain') out of MELODY, and 'Broadcast' rearranges the ELODY left. Read whole, the clue also describes an Alpine call ringing out from a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling Swiss singing style alternating chest and falsetto is traditionally called out across mountain slopes.

clue.text: Question 1: 1000 + 4 2

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
the Roman numeral for a thousand is M

indicators.note: the clue as printed reads 4 / 2, four divided by two, so the 4 down answer is cut in half and its second half dropped

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer to 4 down, the raspberry and ice-cream dessert

explanation.surface: Mimics a maths exam paper: question one sets a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has '4 / 2': half of 4 down's answer, its first five letters. Roman numerals give I and M; '+' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To call into doubt or challenge someone's integrity is to question it; it is also to charge an official formally.

clue.text: Force way into pasty-eating contest after American withdraws

parts.note: a pasty is a kind of pie

indicators.note: withdraws says the abbreviation for American pulls out of the combined pie and contest

parts.note: a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A pie-eating competition carries on after the American competitor drops out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraws' takes the A out of PIE + RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to puncture it, making a hole by forcing a point through.

clue.text: Cry a river inside place that's moving? On the contrary

indicators.note: inside says the river is placed within the cry word

parts.note: to sing out is to cry
the Tay is a Scottish river
to put is to place

explanation.surface: An emotional scene: someone weeping floods of tears in a moving place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry a river' is an idiom for weeping a lot, but here Cry is SING and 'a river' is the Tay in Scotland. 'On the contrary' reverses 'moving' into remaining still.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining where one is means the opposite of moving, which the clue's reversal phrase asks for.

clue.text: Aloof, cutting of course

indicators.note: cutting says the word of is cut out of the aloof word

parts.note: offish means distant or aloof

explanation.surface: Someone stand-offish snubs another person, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' removes OF from OFFISH. 'of course' reads as a stock phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish course is one stage of a formal meal, so the dish names the course.

clue.text: Capital profit's explosive

parts.note: the Smoke is old slang for London, the capital
to make a bomb is to make a large profit

explanation.surface: A financial headline: London's gains are explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is a British nickname for London, and 'a bomb' is British slang for a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that releases a cloud of smoke when set off is a type of explosive.

clue.text: Get off horse, heartlessly kept in stall by whip

indicators.note: by places the whip word beside the stall construction

parts.note: to whip is to beat

indicators.note: kept in says the horse's outer letters are held inside the stall word

parts.note: a trap is a starting stall, as in greyhound racing

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle of horse, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A rider dismounts and the horse is shut in its stall by someone with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves HE from horse; 'kept in' puts it inside TRAP; BEAT goes 'by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaping punishment for a crime is the idiom's sense, so it means get off.

clue.text: Sons of toil who might turn up apt spoonerism?

definitions.meaning: farm labourers are proverbially sons of toil

definitions.text: who might turn up apt spoonerism?
definitions.meaning: the spoonerism of sons of toil is tons of soil, and those who plough turn up tons of soil

explanation.surface: Labourers who might happen upon a witty slip of the tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'sons of toil' gives 'tons of soil', which a ploughing lad literally turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Young farm labourers who drive a plough are sons of toil, working the land.

clue.text: Former dictator regularly overlooked grandad's affair

indicators.note: regularly overlooked says every other letter of grandad's affair is skipped

explanation.surface: A family secret: grandad's fling kept being ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya as an autocrat from 1969 until 2011.

clue.text: Blood oranges exuding scent of Florida

indicators.note: exuding suggests something coming out of the words blood oranges, giving up letters within them

explanation.surface: Blood oranges giving off the aroma of Florida groves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Florida' signals the American spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell or fragrance, spelt the American way as used in a US state like Florida.

clue.text: Covered rise of Northern Ireland party leaders in official report

indicators.note: in a down clue rise of means the Northern Ireland letters are read upwards

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: leaders in takes the first letters of official and report

explanation.surface: An official report covers the rise of a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns NI to IN; 'leaders in' gives O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor describes something under cover, such as an indoor pool with a roof.

clue.text: Revises conclusions about Middle English

indicators.note: about says the conclusions word goes around Middle English

parts.note: ends are conclusions

explanation.surface: A scholar rewrites the conclusions of a paper on Middle English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps ENDS round ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text is to revise it; the verb emend is the editor's term.

clue.text: It's negative to keep finding fault with figure

parts.note: no is a negative
to nag on is to keep criticising

explanation.surface: A grumble that constant criticism of someone is unhelpful.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Looks astonished — beginning and middle transposed in book?

indicators.note: transposed says the beginning and middle letters of the book word swap places

parts.note: a book's contents are on its pages

explanation.surface: A reader stares amazed when the start and middle of a book have been switched.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letter P and the middle letter G of PAGES, as 'beginning and middle transposed' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed in wonder is to look astonished.

clue.text: Expressions of protest and disgust heard through remote connection

indicators.note: heard means the exclamations are spoken out and we take what they sound like

parts.note: why! is a cry of protest and fie an old cry of disgust; said together they form the clue's sound

explanation.surface: Someone shouts complaints down a poor wireless link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns 'why' and 'fie' into the sound of the network term.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless networking links a device to the internet without a cable, a remote connection.

clue.text: He's soon parted from money, backing one that'll scratch

indicators.note: backing tells us the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: the proverb says a fool and his money are soon parted

explanation.surface: A spendthrift backs a horse that will be withdrawn from the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a fool and his money are soon parted' gives A FOOL, reversed by 'backing'. 'scratch' suggests a horse withdrawn from a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried rough sponge from a gourd scrubs the skin when bathing, so it is something abrasive.

clue.text: Spontaneous declaration of support for politician by trade union

indicators.note: by sets the trade union beside the politician

parts.note: saying I'm pro declares support
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An off-the-cuff statement backing a Labour MP from a union.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without preparation or rehearsal, as with an off-the-cuff speech, so unplanned and spontaneous.

clue.text: Enters into difficulty, trapped by bar on legal defence for whistleblowers?

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: trapped by says the rearranged letters go inside the legal word

parts.note: licit means lawful or legal

indicators.note: into difficulty suggests the letters of enters getting into a tangle and rearranging

explanation.surface: A tale of someone stumbling into trouble at a pub, caught on a legal technicality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into difficulty' rearranges ENTERS to NTERES, which LICIT has 'trapped'; PUB comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistleblowers often justify disclosing secrets by claiming the public benefits from knowing.
